findings.problem: The span this milestone covers holds only an instruction note, a printed cue to say the dream prayer, but it gets a `text:` URN. Line 40 lists `instruction` as its own URN type. Its `rosh_hashanah/...` path also sits inside a div whose correspondence is the generic `regalim/...` one. Because of rule 1 (line 179), the div's content scope therefore includes this HE-only cue whenever `kohanim_response_2_5@heidenheim` is resolved or transcluded. The cue is correctly outside every prayer-part, chapter and verse scope, and it is explicitly terminated.
findings.guideline_evidence: Line 40: the hierarchical URN starts with the type of the thing identified ('text', 'note', 'instruction', ...). Line 179: a URN on a non-empty element covers all of its content. Lines 211-213: terminate before unrelated material.
findings.required_change: Check against the existing project convention for navigation milestones; the supplied excerpts do not show one. If there is no established `text:`-typed navigation convention, use an `instruction:` URN for this cue. If the generic regalim div scope must not include it, move the navigation and note outside the div. Make no change to the English file unless the English page actually prints a matching cue (unverified).

verified: 28 files: 14 HE/EN pairs (kohanim_berakhah, kohanim_response_1_1–1_3, 2_1–2_5, 3_1–3_5). Each pair has the same div @corresp and the same prayer-part, chapter and verse milestone @corresp set, apart from the HE-only navigation note in 2_5.

Headers: every idno type='urn' has @project and matches its file's div @corresp. No @corresp anywhere has a project suffix (line 40). sourceDesc uses ptr '/{project}/index#project_source_bibl' with no extension (lines 57-66).
Facsimiles follow page/n(scan−1).jpg under the 146–149 ↔ 312–319 pairing. Page 146: HE n311, EN n312. Page 147: HE n313, EN n314. The div @facs, pb @facs and biblScope agree in every file.
pb n='147' ed='1965' appears only at the start of kohanim_response_3_3, in both HE and EN, before any milestone. It does not split any scope.

Every opened prayer-part, chapter and verse milestone is explicitly terminated inside its own p, inner units first (verse → chapter → prayer-part), per lines 187 and 211-213. No scope relies on a closing p or div tag.

Priest single-word quotations (Num 6:24/25/26) and response verses use quote-context chapter/verse milestones with canonical @n placed before the source-bearing seg (line 219). The contextual corresp paths (…/priest/quotation/numbers/6/24, …/response/quotation/psalms/134/3, and so on) do not reuse the canonical bible URN, so partial words are not advertised as whole verses (lines 223-227).

kohanim_response_3_1 uses the line 220-223 variant: chapter/verse milestones inside seg type='quotation' with canonical @n (Ps 24:5, Prov 3:4), closed before the seg ends, while the enclosing prayer-part correspondence stays outside the seg. Both quoted verses are complete as printed, so the full-verse @source is accurate.
Within each project, the 14 div URNs are distinct and every milestone @corresp is prefixed by its own file's div URN. No duplicate identity was seen within either project.
No English linkage cues, labels or citations are encoded as prayer words in this group. The one instruction (HE 2_5) is a tei:note outside every word scope and has no @rend.
